quizzes.title: Repo Rate and Other Tools
quizzes.passage: Monetary policy is formed and managed by the central bank to control a nation's overall money supply and to achieve economic growth. It differs from fiscal policy, which is managed by the Ministry of Finance and measures spending and taxation in the economy. The Reserve Bank of India releases a Monetary Policy Report once every six months, explaining the sources of inflation and forecasting it for six to eighteen months ahead. The Monetary Policy Committee is chaired by the RBI Governor and determines the policy rate required to achieve the inflation target. The repo rate is the central tool in this framework. When inflation is high, the central bank raises it so that the flow of money in the economy slows down. Borrowing becomes expensive for businesses and industries, investment slows, and excessive spending is curbed. Changes in this rate pass through to the cost of credit across the economy, so lenders and borrowers both feel the effect. The central bank also has other instruments at its disposal. Each of them acts on a different part of the banking system, and each is designed for a specific purpose. Together these tools let the central bank steer liquidity, price stability and growth in the economy, which is the broad aim of monetary policy.

questions.q: What does the 'Repo' in 'repo rate' stand for?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Repo stands for Repurchasing Option or Repurchase Agreement.

questions.q: Which rate is the rate at which RBI borrows money from commercial banks?
questions.explanation: The reverse repo rate is the rate at which RBI borrows money from commercial banks.

questions.q: Which facility allows banks to borrow overnight funds at a rate higher than the repo rate?
questions.explanation: The Marginal Standing Facility is a window for banks to borrow overnight funds at a higher rate than the repo rate.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): RBI lowers the repo rate when it needs to pump funds into the economy during a short-term liquidity crunch.
Reason (R): A lower repo rate makes loans cheaper for banks, which increases the overall supply of money in the economy.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet links a lower repo rate to cheaper loans for banks and a higher supply of money, which is why RBI uses it to pump funds.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: I. Bank Rate   II. Cash Reserve Ratio   III. Statutory Liquidity Ratio   IV. Open market operations
List II: A. Share of deposits banks keep as cash with RBI   B. Long-term rate at which the central bank lends to other banks   C. Purchase or sale of government securities to inject or absorb liquidity   D. Minimum share of deposits held as liquid cash, gold or other securities
questions.explanation: Bank Rate is the long-term lending rate, CRR is the cash share with RBI, SLR is the liquid-holding minimum, and open market operations involve government securities.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. A higher repo rate makes loans costlier for banks.
II. Bank Rate is a short-term rate, while the repo rate is a long-term rate.
III. The Marginal Standing Facility lets banks borrow overnight funds at a rate lower than the repo rate.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since Bank Rate is the long-term rate, the repo rate is the short-term one, and the MSF is priced above the repo rate.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about monetary policy tools are correct?
I. Open market operations are used to inject or absorb liquidity.
II. Bank Rate is a long-term rate at which the central bank lends to other banks.
III. The reverse repo rate is the rate at which RBI lends money to commercial banks.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III reverses the definition of the reverse repo rate.

quizzes.title: Repo Rate and Other Tools
quizzes.passage: The central bank steers the economy through the interest rates it sets, and the repo rate is one of its main tools in this context. When inflation is high, raising the rate makes borrowing expensive, which discourages spending and slows the flow of money in the economy. Monetary policy is formed and managed by the central bank to control a nation's overall money supply and to achieve economic growth. It differs from fiscal policy, which is managed by the Ministry of Finance and measures spending and taxation. The Reserve Bank of India releases a Monetary Policy Report once every six months, explaining the sources of inflation and forecasting it for six to eighteen months ahead. Inflation targeting is a monetary policy framework in which the central bank aims to keep the rate of inflation within a targeted range that is defined in advance. Apart from the repo rate, the central bank has several other instruments, and each of them acts on a different part of the banking system. The central bank uses these tools together to balance liquidity, price stability and growth, which are the goals of monetary policy.

questions.q: What is the abbreviation for the ratio of deposits that banks must hold as cash with the RBI? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: CRR is the proportion of deposits banks must hold as cash with RBI.

questions.q: Which long-term rate, unlike the short-term repo rate, is charged by the central bank when it lends to other banks? (name the rate)
questions.explanation: Bank Rate is the long-term rate at which the central bank lends to other banks.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation MSF stand for? (name the facility)
questions.explanation: MSF is the Marginal Standing Facility, a window for banks to borrow overnight funds.

questions.q: What is the abbreviation for the statutory minimum share of deposits that banks hold as liquid cash, gold or other securities? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: SLR is the Statutory Liquidity Ratio, the minimum share of deposits held as liquid assets.

questions.q: What does the 'Repo' in 'repo rate' stand for? (name the two-word term)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives Repurchasing Option or Repurchase Agreement as the full form of Repo.

questions.q: Which tool involves the buying or selling of government securities to inject or absorb liquidity? (name the tool)
questions.explanation: Open market operations are purchases or sales of government securities used to inject or absorb liquidity.

questions.q: What is the rate at which RBI borrows money from commercial banks called? (name the rate)
questions.explanation: The reverse repo rate is the rate at which RBI borrows money from commercial banks.

quizzes.title: Price Indices and Their Coverage
quizzes.passage: Prices in an economy do not all move together, so official statisticians rely on several indices to track them. Each index is built with its own scope and method. One widely used measure groups household spending into commodity groups such as food, fuel and light, clothing and footwear, housing, pan, tobacco and intoxicants, and miscellaneous items. The same kind of measure also appears in separate versions for agricultural labourers, rural labourers and industrial workers. Each commodity group carries a weight, expressed as a percentage, that determines how much it influences the final figure. A group with a higher weight therefore matters more to the index. The choice of index changes what a number means, so readers must check what each one covers before comparing figures. Some measures capture a broad range of spending, while others rely on a narrower set of items. Two sources that track the same period can therefore show different movements, even when both are official. Knowing what each series includes is the starting point for reading any published price figure.

questions.q: Which year is the base year of the Consumer Price Index?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the CPI base year as 2012.

questions.q: Which body releases the Wholesale Price Index?
options: Office of Economic Advisor, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the WPI is released by the Office of Economic Advisor, Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

questions.q: Which index is described as reflecting up-to-date expenditure patterns?
questions.explanation: The booklet's comparison table says CPI reflects up-to-date expenditure patterns, unlike WPI.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): WPI is a measure of wholesale prices.
Reason (R): WPI includes only goods and does not consider the services sector.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the exclusion of services is a feature of coverage rather than the reason WPI measures wholesale prices.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: I. CPI   II. WPI   III. GDP deflator   IV. Inflation
List II: A. Measures inflation in the retail market   B. Compares annual production value at current prices with a base year   C. Increase in overall prices of goods and services over time   D. Includes only goods and reflects wholesale prices
questions.explanation: CPI measures retail inflation, WPI covers only goods at wholesale prices, the GDP deflator compares production at current prices with a base year, and inflation is a rise in overall prices.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. CPI includes both goods and services.
II. WPI is released by the National Statistical Office.
III. Inflation is a fall in the overall prices of goods and services over time.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since WPI is released by the Office of Economic Advisor and inflation is a rise in prices, not a fall.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about price indices are correct?
I. Inflation refers to an increase in the overall prices of goods and services in an economy over time.
II. CPI is released by the Office of Economic Advisor.
III. GDP deflator measures wholesale prices alone.
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since CPI is released by the NSO and the GDP deflator is not limited to wholesale prices.

quizzes.title: Price Indices and Their Coverage
quizzes.passage: Price movements in an economy are followed through statistical indices rather than through a single figure. An index tracks a set of goods and services over time and compares their prices with those in a chosen base period. Each item in the set is given a weight, usually expressed as a percentage, which shows how much that item contributes to the final number. Because the set of items and the weights differ from one index to another, the same economy can present different figures depending on the index used. One index breaks household spending into groups such as food, fuel and light, clothing and footwear, housing, and miscellaneous items, each with its own percentage weight. The publishing body and the method note therefore matter as much as the headline value. A reader who wishes to compare two numbers should first check which goods and services each index includes, whether the index covers services, and which period is treated as the reference. Changes measured from the base period are read as movements in the index, and a rise or fall in the value shows how the set of items has moved. Careful readers therefore look at coverage, weights and reference period together before deciding what a change in an index means.

questions.q: What is the base year of the Consumer Price Index? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the CPI base year as 2012.

questions.q: Which agency releases the Consumer Price Index? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the CPI is released by the National Statistical Office (NSO).

questions.q: Under which ministry does the Office of Economic Advisor, which releases the WPI, function? (name the ministry)
questions.explanation: The Office of Economic Advisor is part of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, as the booklet states.

questions.q: Which index covers only goods and does not consider the services sector? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the WPI includes only goods and does not consider the services sector.

questions.q: What is the name of the measure that compares annual production value at current prices with a base year? (name)
questions.explanation: The GDP deflator compares annual production value at current prices with a base year.

questions.q: Which index has separate versions for agricultural labourers, rural labourers and industrial workers? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists CPI-AL, CPI-RL and CPI-IW as separate versions of the consumer price index.

questions.q: What is the term for an increase in the overall prices of goods and services in an economy over time? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet defines inflation as an increase in the overall prices of goods and services in an economy over time.

quizzes.title: Origins and Functions of the RBI
quizzes.passage: The Reserve Bank of India is the institution that the country relies on for managing its financial system. Its role has grown over time, and it now touches the government, the banking sector and the wider public. The Bank sets policy and keeps watch over the institutions that carry it out. Among its responsibilities it holds and manages the foreign exchange reserves that the country maintains. The Bank was created after a period of official consideration, under a law passed when the country was under foreign rule. Its work is defined by statute, and that statute gives it powers over money and banking. Monetary policy, which the Bank manages, differs from fiscal policy handled by the Ministry of Finance, which deals with government spending and taxation. The Bank publishes a Monetary Policy Report once every six months to explain the sources of inflation. The Bank's presence is felt in everyday finance, through the notes people carry, the rates banks charge and the rules that govern the wider system.

questions.q: Which commission recommended the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Hilton Young Commission recommended the creation of the RBI.

questions.q: Dr. Ambedkar's strategies, set out in his book on the rupee, inspired the concept of which institution?
options: The Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.explanation: The booklet says the RBI's concept was inspired by Dr. Ambedkar's strategies in his book on the rupee.

questions.q: On what date was the Reserve Bank of India established?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the RBI was established on April 1 in Calcutta.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The RBI acts as banker to the Government of India.
Reason (R): The RBI manages all financial operations of the Central Government under the RBI Act of 1934.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and managing the government's financial operations is the reason the RBI serves as its banker.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
List I: I. Supervisory function   II. Issuer of currency   III. Monetary authority   IV. Lender of last resort
List II: A. Maintaining price stability while promoting economic growth   B. Authority to issue bank licences, open branches and inspect banks   C. Exchanging and destroying currency notes   D. Providing support to banks as the lender of last resort
questions.explanation: Supervisory function covers licences and inspections, issuer of currency covers exchanging and destroying notes, monetary authority covers price stability, and the lender of last resort role is D.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The RBI is the custodian of the cash reserves of commercial banks.
II. The RBI has been privately owned since its establishment.
III. The RBI intervenes to stabilise USD/INR currency volatility.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is false because the RBI was nationalised after being owned by private stakeholders.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the RBI are correct?
I. The RBI can grant bank licences and inspect commercial banks.
II. The RBI's concept was inspired by a book written by Mahatma Gandhi.
III. The RBI regulates the forex market through exchange rules.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is false because the booklet credits Dr. Ambedkar's book.

quizzes.title: Origins and Functions of the RBI
quizzes.passage: The Reserve Bank of India sits at the centre of the country's financial system. The institution was not always under public control, since it began with private stakeholders before the state took over. It was set up under a law passed by the British government and began operating in an eastern city, on a fixed day of the year. Its tasks are varied. It grants bank licences, approves the opening of branches and inspects banks. In the foreign exchange area it holds the country's reserves, manages its dealings and enforces exchange rules. It also manages the financial affairs of the central government and provides advances to state governments through agreements. The Bank acts as a banker to other banks and to the government. Monetary policy, which the Bank manages, differs from fiscal policy handled by the Ministry of Finance. The Bank also publishes a Monetary Policy Report and intervenes to limit volatility in the rupee against the dollar. Together these roles make the Bank a central point of the country's money and banking system.

questions.q: Which commission recommended the establishment of the RBI? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Hilton Young Commission recommended the creation of the RBI.

questions.q: In which city was the RBI established? (name the city)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the RBI was established on April 1 in Calcutta.

questions.q: On which day and month was the RBI established? (day and month)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives April 1 as the date on which the RBI was established.

questions.q: Dr. Ambedkar's book, whose ideas inspired the RBI's concept, has what title? (name the title)
accept: The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Its Solution
The Problem of the Rupee - Its Origin and Its Solution
questions.explanation: The booklet names Dr. Ambedkar's book as The Problem of the Rupee, Its Origin and Its Solution.

questions.q: The RBI acts as custodian of the cash reserves of which institutions? (name, two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the RBI as custodian of the cash reserves of commercial banks.

questions.q: What is the name of the RBI's role of formulating policy to keep prices steady while promoting growth? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the RBI as the monetary authority, which aims to maintain price stability while promoting economic growth.

questions.q: What is the name of the function under which the RBI exchanges and destroys currency notes? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the RBI's role of exchanging and destroying currency notes under the issuer of currency function.
